title: I couldn't get 19 AI-generated goblins to look like the same game — until I stopped generating characters and started deriving them
author: Joeykiwis

comments.author: Joeykiwis
comments.body: Tool used is PixelLab — happy to share exact prompts if useful

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
Nice! I like. 
I have a pipeline where I try to achieve that locally but it's not that good yet. 

Can I see the goblin master prompt?

replies.author: Joeykiwis
replies.body:
Sure! There's no single "master prompt" — the anchor is a saved *character*, not text (that's kind of the post's thesis). What's constant is the edit template every goblin derivation uses:

    give it <ROLE EQUIPMENT>, keep the same small goblin body,
    big pointy ears, chunky cute flat pixel style and green skin,
    front view facing camera, <role name>

with the tool's `use_color_palette_from_reference = true` — honestly that palette lock did more for consistency than any wording.

Real `<ROLE EQUIPMENT>` values I shipped with, verbatim:

* shield-bearer: `large round wooden shield and a short sword, defensive stance`
* merchant: `bulging loot sack and a coin pouch, no weapon, greedy grin`
* shaman: `hood and a skull-topped staff with bone fetishes`
* gunner: `crude hand-cannon blunderbuss, makeshift metal, smoke`
* butcher (elite): `bigger and hulking, giant bloody cleaver and a blood-stained apron`
* warchief (boss): `larger and imposing, skull helmet, big battle-axe and war trophies`

Note how short they are — just equipment + one pose/mood word. Every time I added atmosphere adjectives ("fierce", "menacing") things drifted. Size words ("bigger and hulking") are the one exception; they work great for elites while keeping the family resemblance.

If your local pipeline is SD-based, the closest equivalent to this setup is a reference/IP-Adapter image + palette lock, with the prompt reduced to just the diff.

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
Great! 
Have you tried creating equipment separately?

replies.author: Joeykiwis
replies.body: I tried — but the moment you animate, re-attaching separate equipment to every frame becomes its own job (9 frames × 19 enemies). With AI gen it ended up easier to bake the equipment into the character and let the animation handle everything as one piece. Modular gear would pay off if enemies swapped outfits, but mine never change clothes :)

comments.author: thewowcollector
comments.body: I tried using that, and it just kept changing the looks a little. Scenario was great on the $45 plan until it started saying generations would be 13 tokens, and then turned into 350. Your results look great so far

replies.author: Joeykiwis
replies.body:
The "keeps changing a little" thing bit me too — two things fixed most of it:

1. **Always derive from the anchor, never from a derivative.** Early on I'd edit the shaman to make the fanatic, and drift compounded with every hop. Now all 18 goblins are *siblings* branching off the one anchor — flat tree, no chains. Drift stopped accumulating.
2. Palette lock + keeping the edit to just the equipment diff. If a result still drifts, I don't retry with more words — I re-derive with fewer.

And ouch, 13 → 350 tokens is brutal. PixelLab's pain is different (queue times got up to 60–90 min at peak), but at least the pricing didn't move under me mid-project.

So what are you working with these days — still Scenario, or did you move to something else? Would love to see what you've made with it if you have anything shareable.

replies.author: thewowcollector
replies.body: I was working mainly with backgrounds, because I couldnt get something more reliable. I will DM you and let you check em out.

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
Doesn't share the workflow, promises of magical results, every post and comment reads like raw Claude output.  Just waiting for a comment to tell me what part of this is "real belt and suspenders"

Wish this sub would crack down on the thinly veiled advertisements.

replies.author: Joeykiwis
replies.body:
Fair to be skeptical, but genuinely — what's being advertised? There's no game name, no link, nothing for sale anywhere in the post. The prompts in the comments are copy-pasted from my actual work notes.

You're right about one thing though: I'm Korean, my English is rough, so I do run my drafts through an LLM before posting here. The sprites, the failures, and the three days are mine. If there's a specific part you think is fake, ask — I'll show receipts.
